meta.title: Navitas Semiconductor — Gene Sheridan's GaN-and-SiC power pure-play through the 800V AI data centre cycle
meta.abstract: Navitas Semiconductor is a gallium nitride (GaN) and silicon carbide (SiC) power semiconductor pure-play listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVTS. Founded in 2014 by Gene Sheridan and Dan Kinzer (former International Rectifier executives) and headquartered in Torrance, California, Navitas brought to market the GaNFast monolithic integrated GaN power IC platform that combines a GaN power FET with the gate driver and protection circuitry on a single chip. The company completed its NASDAQ listing in October 2021 through a SPAC merger with Live Oak Acquisition Corp II at an enterprise value of approximately $1 billion. The 2022-2024 period saw the broader GaN product portfolio scaling across the mobile fast-charger, data centre, solar, electric vehicle, and broader power applications, the August 2022 acquisition of GeneSiC Semiconductor adding the silicon carbide (SiC) power device portfolio at approximately $215 million in equity consideration, and the broader strategic positioning evolution. The 2024-2025 period was substantially defined by the announced strategic partnership with Nvidia (December 2024) for next-generation 800V high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) power architecture supporting Nvidia AI data centre deployments. The 800V HVDC architecture provides substantial power efficiency improvements over the traditional 48V architecture in hyperscaler AI data centre power infrastructure. Under co-founder and CEO Gene Sheridan, the strategic mandate has been the broader GaN and SiC product portfolio scaling, the 800V AI data centre opportunity development through the Nvidia partnership, and the broader operational execution toward profitability.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## The Real Inflection Arrived in May 2025

Navitas Semiconductor was founded in 2014 by Gene Sheridan and Dan Kinzer, both veterans of International Rectifier, around a simple thesis: gallium nitride could displace silicon in large parts of power conversion if the device, driver and protection functions were integrated into a single power IC rather than sold as a loose collection of parts. When Navitas agreed to merge with Live Oak Acquisition Corp. II in May 2021, the company told investors that it had commercialised that monolithic approach through its GaNFast product family and that the transaction implied an enterprise value of about $1.04 billion. The merger closed on October 19, 2021, and Navitas began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol NVTS. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power) [Closing 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465921127670/tm2129072d1_8k.htm)

The company's second structural move came in August 2022, when it completed the acquisition of GeneSiC Semiconductor. The headline was not an all-stock $215 million deal, as earlier summaries had suggested. Navitas said the consideration consisted of about $100 million in cash, 24,883,161 Navitas shares and an earn-out of up to $25 million tied to 2022 revenue targets; its 2025 Form 10-K later put total merger consideration at about $246.2 million. The acquisition gave Navitas a silicon-carbide portfolio alongside GaN and brought GeneSiC founder Ranbir Singh into the company. [GeneSiC completion release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-completes-acquisition-genesic-semiconductor) [2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176926000007/nvts-20251231.htm)

## The Revenue Arc Was Later and Lower Than the Draft Claimed

The operating history looked different once it was checked against the company's filings and annual releases:

| Period | Revenue (USD millions) | Primary source |
|---|---:|---|
| 2021 | 23.7 | [2023 Form 10-K](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/7f0b5a20-3e32-44fc-96c7-710c0ee8ae26) |
| 2022 | 37.9 | [FY2022 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) |
| 2023 | 79.5 | [FY2024 results, comparative disclosure](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) |
| 2024 | 83.3 | [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) |
| 2025 | 45.9 | [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) |
| Q1 2026 | 8.6 | [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial) |

That matters because the old draft had treated 2023 as a $93 million peak and 2024 as the start of contraction. The primary record showed something else: 2024 was still a record revenue year at $83.3 million, fourth-quarter 2024 revenue was $18.0 million, year-end 2024 cash stood at $86.7 million, and management said the company had booked more than $450 million of design wins while GaN and SiC products had started shipping into data-centre applications in the second half. The hard reset came in 2025, when Navitas deliberately shed lower-margin mobile fast-charger distribution business under what it branded Navitas 2.0. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

## NVIDIA Was a May 2025 Disclosure, Not a December 2024 One

The most important customer-facing announcement inside the frozen window was made on May 21, 2025, when NVIDIA said it had selected Navitas to collaborate on next-generation 800V HVDC architecture for Kyber rack-scale systems powering Rubin Ultra GPUs. The release was unusually specific for a semiconductor design announcement: NVIDIA and Navitas said the 800V architecture could improve end-to-end power efficiency by as much as 5 per cent, cut power-supply maintenance costs by as much as 70 per cent and reduce copper needs by as much as 45 per cent versus 54V systems. Navitas positioned its role as spanning the chain from grid to GPU, using GaNSafe power ICs and high-voltage SiC devices. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

Public disclosures then showed the collaboration moving from architecture talk to hardware. In October 2025 Navitas said it was supporting NVIDIA's next-generation 800VDC architecture with medium-voltage 100V GaN, 650V GaN and high-voltage SiC technologies. In the fourth-quarter 2025 release, management said it had accelerated customer sampling of 100V and new 650V GaN solutions for AI-data-centre 800V HVDC architecture, had announced an all-GaN 10 kW 800V-to-50V platform at up to 98.5 per cent peak efficiency, and had accelerated sampling of new 2300V and 3300V SiC products. In the first-quarter 2026 release, management said it had shown a 20 kW 800V HVDC to 6V DC-DC power delivery board at NVIDIA GTC and a 250 kW solid-state transformer in partnership with EPFL. [October 2025 NVIDIA update](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-supports-800-vdc-power-architecture-nvidias-next) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## Capital, Cash and the 2025 Reset

The financial bridge for that pivot was explicit. Navitas sold 14,814,813 common shares in a private placement announced on November 7, 2025 at $6.75 a share for gross proceeds of about $100 million and expected net proceeds of about $95.6 million. At year-end 2025, the company reported $236.9 million of cash and cash equivalents and no debt; by March 31, 2026, cash and cash equivalents had fallen to $221.0 million. The first-quarter release guided second-quarter revenue to $10.0 million plus or minus $0.5 million. [Private placement 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465925096333/tm2528557d1_8k.htm) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The mix shift also showed up in the disclosures. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Navitas said mobile and consumer had fallen to less than 25 per cent of revenue while high-power markets had risen to more than 50 per cent. In the first quarter of 2026, management said high-power markets represented a large majority of revenue and had grown 35 per cent year on year; Stevens said the quarter also reflected expanded customer engagements and order backlog. Non-GAAP gross margin moved from 38.7 per cent in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 39.0 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while GAAP operating loss improved from $41.4 million in the fourth quarter to $27.8 million in the first quarter. The company remained deeply loss-making, but the operating narrative had clearly shifted from consumer chargers to infrastructure power. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## Management Changed More Sharply Than the Earlier Draft Allowed

The leadership story also needed correction. Dan Kinzer did not remain in place as COO and CTO through the transition. Navitas disclosed that he resigned from his executive roles effective May 1, 2025 and resigned from the board effective May 8, 2025, while remaining for a short period as an adviser and consultant focused on GaN technology. Gene Sheridan later stepped down as chief executive and from the board effective August 31, 2025. Chris Allexandre, who had run Renesas's power division, became president and chief executive on September 1, 2025. The finance seat changed too: Todd Glickman resigned effective March 30, 2026, and Tonya Stevens, previously Navitas's chief accounting officer, became senior vice-president of finance and chief financial officer the same day. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) [Allexandre appointment release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-names-chris-allexandre-president-and-chief) [Tonya Stevens 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926026385/tm268482d1_8k.htm) [Todd Glickman 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926029469/tm269070d1_8k.htm)

## The Questions Left Open by the Frozen Window

By the frozen snapshot date of May 23, 2026, the dossier's central issue was no longer whether Navitas had found a new story. It had. The open question was whether the story would convert into booked, recurring revenue fast enough to justify the reset. Public disclosures through the first-quarter 2026 release showed collaboration with NVIDIA, development hardware, a new foundry strategy, a cleaner end-market mix and compensation incentives that were explicitly tied to future revenue goals. They did not disclose a commercial contract value, a named backlog figure tied to NVIDIA, or a dated revenue ramp attributable to that programme. That left the case resting on primary evidence of strategic position rather than on primary evidence of scaled monetisation. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc) [October 2025 NVIDIA update](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-supports-800-vdc-power-architecture-nvidias-next) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial) [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

chapters.title: From 2014 Torrance founding through SPAC, GeneSiC, NVIDIA, and Allexandre
chapters.body:
## A Founding Thesis Built Around Monolithic GaN

Navitas was founded in 2014 in Torrance, California by Gene Sheridan and Dan Kinzer after long careers at International Rectifier. In the investor materials used for the 2021 SPAC transaction, the company said it had created the first monolithically integrated GaN power IC, combining the GaN power device with drive, control and protection functions on the same platform rather than asking customers to assemble those pieces themselves. That architectural choice defined the company from the start and remained the through-line of the story even after the later addition of silicon carbide. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power)

The manufacturing model was set early as well. In 2017 Navitas announced manufacturing partnerships with TSMC for wafer fabrication and Amkor for packaging, giving the company a fabless route to volume production without building its own plants. That was a practical decision as much as a financial one: Navitas was trying to commercialise a new power architecture inside an industry that was still dominated by silicon incumbents, and it could not afford both process development and a captive fab strategy. [TSMC and Amkor manufacturing release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-announces-tsmc-amkor-manufacturing-partnerships)

## The First Commercial Arc Was Consumer Power

The early commercial wedge was the power adapter. The SPAC materials listed a customer and partner set that included Dell, Lenovo, LG, Xiaomi, OPPO, Amazon and Belkin, evidence that Navitas had already turned GaNFast into real design wins across notebook, mobile and consumer power products before coming public. By the time the company closed its merger with Live Oak on October 19, 2021, it had reported 2021 revenue of $23.7 million. That rose to $37.9 million in 2022 as mobile fast-charging adoption broadened. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power) [Closing 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465921127670/tm2129072d1_8k.htm) [FY2022 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year)

That first arc was later and smaller than the old draft suggested. Primary disclosures did not support a $93 million 2023 revenue peak. The official comparison in the 2024 annual results release showed 2023 revenue at $79.5 million and 2024 revenue at $83.3 million. The point is important because it changes the shape of the history: 2024 was not the beginning of a revenue collapse but the last year of the original growth model, with record design wins and the first disclosed shipments into data-centre applications in the second half. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year)

## GeneSiC Turned Navitas Into a Two-Material Company

The decisive expansion came on August 15, 2022, when Navitas completed the acquisition of GeneSiC Semiconductor. The company described GeneSiC as a specialist in silicon-carbide power semiconductors and said the acquired business added high-voltage SiC capabilities across diodes, MOSFETs and related power applications. The economics also changed the balance sheet more than earlier drafts acknowledged: the deal used about $100 million of cash, 24,883,161 Navitas shares and an earn-out of up to $25 million, with later SEC disclosure putting total consideration at about $246.2 million. [GeneSiC completion release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-completes-acquisition-genesic-semiconductor) [2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176926000007/nvts-20251231.htm)

That move broadened the product story from a GaN specialist into a wide-bandgap supplier that could cover both the fast-switching, lower-voltage layers of power conversion and the higher-voltage nodes where SiC had structural advantages. It also brought Ranbir Singh, GeneSiC's founder, into the leadership orbit and later onto the board. The company would use that dual-material identity repeatedly in later data-centre and industrial messaging. [GeneSiC completion release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-completes-acquisition-genesic-semiconductor) [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

## The NVIDIA Milestone Came in 2025

The dossier's earlier timeline had put the NVIDIA inflection in December 2024. The primary record placed it on May 21, 2025, when NVIDIA said it had selected Navitas to collaborate on 800V HVDC power architecture for Kyber rack-scale systems powering Rubin Ultra GPUs. That announcement mattered not because it instantly created disclosed revenue, but because it repositioned Navitas from a company associated chiefly with power adapters and chargers to one participating in the architecture discussion around AI infrastructure power delivery. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

The company's own releases around that date showed that the operating strategy was already changing. In April 2025 Navitas announced partnerships with Great Wall and GigaDevice, both tied to higher-power or system-level applications rather than handset chargers. In July 2025 it announced a 200 mm manufacturing relationship with Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation, explicitly linking that foundry move to data centres, electric vehicles and solar. In November 2025 it announced a strategic partnership with GlobalFoundries for U.S.-based GaN manufacturing. The broad pattern was that the customer and manufacturing stack was being rebuilt for infrastructure markets rather than consumer accessories. [Great Wall release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-partners-great-wall-next-generation-400v-dc-power) [GigaDevice release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-gigadevice-announce-partnership-combine-power-control) [PSMC release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/cbb9fa0e-1a41-463e-b71c-1a5b1145678d) [GlobalFoundries partnership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000217/nvts-20251120.htm)

## The Company Entered 2026 as a Reset, Not a Straight-Line Grower

The financials completed the historical arc. Revenue fell to $45.9 million in 2025 as Navitas exited lower-margin mobile distribution channels under Navitas 2.0. In the fourth quarter of 2025, management said mobile and consumer had fallen below a quarter of revenue while high-power markets had risen above half. The first quarter of 2026 then produced $8.6 million of revenue, up 18 per cent sequentially from the fourth-quarter trough, with high-power markets described as a large majority of the mix. In other words, the historical chapter that ended the frozen window was not one of uninterrupted scaling. It was one of deliberate self-disruption in pursuit of a different customer base. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

chapters.title: GaNFast platform, SiC portfolio, mobile-to-AI segment pivot
chapters.body:
## GaNFast Remained the Core Product Idea

Navitas's business still began with GaNFast. On its product pages and in its public filings, the company described GaNFast as a monolithically integrated GaN power IC family that combined power, drive, control, sensing and protection functions. That integration mattered commercially because it let customers design smaller, faster-switching and more efficient power systems without having to assemble a discrete GaN bill of materials themselves. The company built its earliest revenue around low- and mid-power consumer and mobile chargers, then extended the same design philosophy upward into data-centre, solar and industrial applications. [GaN power IC platform](https://navitassemi.com/gan-power-ics/) [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power)

The official product story also showed how Navitas wanted investors to think about the portfolio by 2025 and 2026. Consumer-adapter applications remained part of the installed base, but the company's releases increasingly highlighted 650V GaN and higher-power system designs rather than USB charger miniaturisation. That rhetorical shift matched the financial one described elsewhere in the dossier: the company was trying to move from high-volume, lower-margin consumer sockets to fewer but richer infrastructure and industrial sockets. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## GaNSafe Was the Bridge Into Higher Power

In April 2025, Navitas announced automotive qualification for its high-power GaNSafe ICs. The company said the family combined control, drive, sensing and critical protection features and had achieved both AEC-Q100 and AEC-Q101 qualification, which gave the portfolio a level of external validation beyond internal marketing language. That announcement mattered because it showed the company had moved from telling a pure speed-and-density story to telling a reliability story as well. High-power customers, particularly in automotive, data-centre and industrial power, cared less about novelty than about protection, repeatability and qualification discipline. [GaNSafe automotive qualification release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-announces-automotive-qualification-high-power-gansafetm)

The role of GaNSafe in the broader business mix became clearer in the NVIDIA disclosures. In the May 2025 collaboration release, Navitas said it would combine GaNSafe power ICs with high-voltage SiC devices across the 800V HVDC chain. In October 2025 the company sharpened that message by saying it was supporting NVIDIA's next-generation 800VDC architecture with medium-voltage 100V GaN, 650V GaN and high-voltage SiC. The segment story was no longer about one GaN family selling into one charger class; it was about stacked device layers inside larger power systems. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc) [October 2025 NVIDIA update](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-supports-800-vdc-power-architecture-nvidias-next)

## GeneSiC Added the Higher-Voltage Side of the Ladder

The GeneSiC acquisition gave Navitas a second material system and a second set of end markets. The acquisition release described GeneSiC as a silicon-carbide specialist with products spanning SiC MOSFETs, Schottky diodes and related power devices. By 2025 and 2026, Navitas was publicly pairing those devices with its GaN products in a single architectural pitch: GaN for the higher-frequency switching stages, SiC for the higher-voltage nodes where efficiency and ruggedness mattered more than absolute switching speed. [GeneSiC completion release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-completes-acquisition-genesic-semiconductor) [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

That dual-material stack was visible again at PCIM Europe in May 2025, where Navitas said it would showcase production-released 650V bi-directional GaNFast ICs, a new IsoFast family and GeneSiC's trench-assisted planar SiC MOSFETs in SiCPAK power modules. The event release did not break out revenue by product family, but it made the company's portfolio logic easy to read: Navitas no longer wanted to be analysed as a charger-chip vendor with a side acquisition. It wanted to be analysed as a wide-bandgap platform vendor able to place different devices at different points in the same conversion chain. [PCIM 2025 release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-showcases-advances-gan-and-sic-technologies-including)

## The End-Market Mix Shifted Faster Than the Revenue Line

The cleanest way to describe the segment evolution was not with unsupported historical percentages, but with the milestones that management actually disclosed:

| Period | What management disclosed about mix |
|---|---|
| FY2024 | More than $450 million of design wins; GaN and SiC products started shipping into data-centre applications in H2 2024. |
| Q4 2025 | Mobile and consumer fell to less than 25 per cent of revenue; high-power markets rose to more than 50 per cent. |
| Q1 2026 | High-power markets represented a large majority of revenue and grew 35 per cent year on year. |

The effect was that Navitas's operating identity changed before its reported scale recovered. By the first quarter of 2026, the company was still reporting only $8.6 million of quarterly revenue, but the disclosed mix was already dominated by the markets management wanted investors to underwrite: AI data centres, energy and green infrastructure, performance computing and industrial electrification. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

That four-market taxonomy matters because it replaced the older mental model of Navitas as a consumer-adapter specialist. The first-quarter 2026 release explicitly grouped the opportunity into AI data centres, energy and green infrastructure, performance computing and industrial electrification. Combined with the 2024 disclosure that GaN revenue had risen more than 50 per cent to a record high even before the channel reset, the segment story became one of redeployment rather than abandonment: Navitas was trying to carry the integration advantages learned in consumer power into larger and more qualification-intensive systems. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## The Product Roadmap Was Starting to Look Like Infrastructure, Not Adapters

The fourth-quarter 2025 and first-quarter 2026 releases added an important layer of specificity. In the February 2026 results, Navitas said it had accelerated customer sampling of 100V and new 650V GaN solutions for AI-data-centre 800V HVDC architecture and 48V intermediate-bus buck architecture, announced an all-GaN 10 kW 800V-to-50V DC-DC platform at up to 98.5 per cent peak efficiency, and accelerated sampling of 2300V and 3300V ultra-high-voltage SiC products. In May 2026 it followed with the 20 kW 800V-to-6V power-delivery board at up to 97.5 per cent peak efficiency and a 250 kW solid-state transformer using 3300V and 1200V GeneSiC devices. Those were not abstract roadmaps; they were concrete prototypes and sample programmes aimed squarely at rack power, grid infrastructure and industrial electrification. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## The Architecture Was Becoming More System-Level

The surrounding ecosystem announcements supported that reading. Great Wall's next-generation 400V DC power architecture for AI data centres used Navitas's GaNFast ICs in a 2.5 kW DC-DC converter. GigaDevice agreed with Navitas to build a joint lab and pursue combined power-and-control solutions. The 20 kW 800V HVDC to 6V board shown at NVIDIA GTC in 2026 suggested Navitas wanted to prove that its devices belonged in complete rack-level power chains, not just in isolated converter blocks. Those were still development and platform signals rather than disclosed multi-year customer contracts, but they showed clearly where the segment strategy was pointed. [Great Wall release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-partners-great-wall-next-generation-400v-dc-power) [GigaDevice release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-gigadevice-announce-partnership-combine-power-control) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, Navitas 2.0 restructuring, and cash runway
chapters.body:
## The Reported Numbers Showed a Reset, Not a Steady Climb

Navitas's financial story through the frozen window made sense only once the annual numbers were corrected. Revenue moved from $23.7 million in 2021 to $37.9 million in 2022, then to $79.5 million in 2023 and a record $83.3 million in 2024 before dropping to $45.9 million in 2025. The earlier draft had overstated 2023 revenue and turned 2024 into the start of the decline. The primary record showed that the sharp break came in 2025, after management decided to shed lower-margin mobile distribution business and rebuild the mix around high-power markets. [2023 Form 10-K](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/7f0b5a20-3e32-44fc-96c7-710c0ee8ae26) [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

The 2024 baseline was also stronger and more visible than the old version allowed. Navitas reported fourth-quarter 2024 revenue of $18.0 million, full-year GAAP loss from operations of $130.7 million, full-year non-GAAP loss from operations of $49.7 million and year-end cash of $86.7 million. The company was not yet profitable even in the last year of the old model, but it did still have a growing revenue line and a large design-win pipeline. That made 2025 a deliberate break with the previous operating pattern rather than a continuation of it. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year)

The quarterly progression in 2025 showed that reset happening in real time:

| Quarter | Revenue (USD millions) | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Q1 2025 | 14.0 | [Q1 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2025-financial) |
| Q2 2025 | 14.5 | [Q2 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-second-quarter-2025-financial) |
| Q3 2025 | 10.1 | [Q3 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-third-quarter-2025-financial) |
| Q4 2025 | 7.3 | [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) |
| Q1 2026 | 8.6 | [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial) |

The sequence mattered because management did not present the 2025 collapse as an unexplained demand hole. It presented it as the cost of abandoning revenue that it no longer wanted. In the 2025 annual release, the company said the fourth quarter represented the trough, with mobile and consumer under a quarter of revenue and high-power over half. The first quarter of 2026 then came in 18 per cent above that trough, with high-power a large majority of the mix. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## Margin Moved the Right Way, Even if Scale Did Not

The gross-margin line was one of the few places where the restructuring showed up quickly. Navitas reported non-GAAP gross margin of 38.7 per cent in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 39.0 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. That was still modest for a mature fabless analogue or power-semiconductor company, but it was directionally consistent with the thesis that infrastructure and industrial sockets would be structurally better than mobile distribution revenue. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The profit-and-loss statement nevertheless remained heavy. In the 2025 Form 10-K, Navitas disclosed $18.0 million of charges tied to restructuring activity during 2025, including $16.6 million associated with the Navitas 2.0 plan and $1.4 million tied to a separate 2025 restructuring plan. The company reported a GAAP operating loss of $41.4 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and a GAAP operating loss of $27.8 million in the first quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed from $12.1 million in the fourth quarter to $11.7 million in the first quarter, which was progress, but it was progress on a still-loss-making base. [2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176926000007/nvts-20251231.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

That first-quarter release also supplied a more granular view of where the cost structure sat. Research and development expense was $14.6 million, selling, general and administrative expense was $11.3 million, amortisation of intangible assets was $4.7 million and total operating expenses were $31.0 million. In other words, the company had restored sequential revenue growth without yet materially shrinking the fixed operating base that had to be supported. [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## Cash Was Raised Twice and Then Consumed Predictably

The capital structure changed materially during the period. In the second quarter of 2025, Navitas said it had raised about $100 million of additional capital through the sale of roughly 20 million common shares, using that financing to strengthen the balance sheet and support the wider reset. It then returned to the market in November 2025 with a private placement of 14,814,813 common shares at $6.75 each, for gross proceeds of about $100 million and expected net proceeds of $95.6 million. Those transactions helped lift year-end cash and cash equivalents to $236.9 million. By the end of the first quarter of 2026, cash had fallen to $221.0 million. [Q2 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-second-quarter-2025-financial) [Private placement 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465925096333/tm2528557d1_8k.htm) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The dilution showed up in the share counts. The first-quarter 2026 release listed weighted-average diluted shares of 229.988 million, up from 222.344 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 187.784 million in the first quarter of 2025. Stockholders' equity at December 31, 2025 was $443.7 million, up from $348.0 million a year earlier, which underlined how heavily the reset was financed by the equity cushion rather than by internally generated cash. [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

## The Financial Question Became One of Conversion

By the frozen snapshot date, the narrow accounting question was straightforward: could $221.0 million of cash carry Navitas far enough for the high-power segment to scale before another large financing round became necessary. The broader financial question was tougher. Public disclosures had established a plausible chain of milestones: more than $450 million of design wins in 2024, the NVIDIA architecture collaboration in May 2025, a Powerchip foundry relationship in July 2025, a GlobalFoundries partnership in November 2025, and a 20 kW demonstration board at GTC in 2026. What they had not established was a disclosed revenue bridge from those milestones to anything like the historical peak revenue base, let alone to profitability. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc) [PSMC release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/cbb9fa0e-1a41-463e-b71c-1a5b1145678d) [GlobalFoundries partnership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000217/nvts-20251120.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

chapters.title: Post-SPAC quarters through NVIDIA partnership and Allexandre era
chapters.body:
## The Earnings Story Broke Into Two Distinct Acts

The first act was the charger-and-adapter build-out. Revenue rose from $23.7 million in 2021 to $37.9 million in 2022 as Navitas scaled GaNFast across consumer power applications, then to $79.5 million in 2023 and a record $83.3 million in 2024. The corrected numbers mattered because they showed the original model still working through 2024, even as the company was already preparing to pivot. [2023 Form 10-K](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/7f0b5a20-3e32-44fc-96c7-710c0ee8ae26) [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year)

That first act was not especially profitable, but it was commercially legible. In the 2024 annual results, Navitas reported fourth-quarter revenue of $18.0 million, year-end cash of $86.7 million and more than $450 million of design wins, while saying GaN and SiC had started shipping into data-centre applications in the second half of the year. The company had, in other words, both a functioning consumer business and an emerging infrastructure angle before the formal reset. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year)

The second act was Navitas 2.0. Revenue fell to $45.9 million in 2025, and quarterly sales stepped down from $14.0 million in the first quarter to $7.3 million in the fourth quarter as management exited lower-margin mobile distribution channels. That decline was painful, but it was not hidden. The company said directly that the fourth quarter represented the trough and that the reset had shifted the mix decisively toward high-power markets. [Q1 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2025-financial) [Q2 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-second-quarter-2025-financial) [Q3 2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-third-quarter-2025-financial) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

The most consequential announcement during that second act came on May 21, 2025, when NVIDIA said it had selected Navitas to collaborate on its 800V HVDC architecture for Kyber rack-scale systems powering Rubin Ultra GPUs. That release did not disclose a contract value, but it changed the company's external positioning and gave management a credible anchor for the shift away from chargers and toward infrastructure. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

The first quarter of 2026 was then the first quarter that read like a test of the new model rather than an unwind of the old one. Revenue was $8.6 million, up 18 per cent sequentially; non-GAAP gross margin was 39.0 per cent; high-power markets were a large majority of revenue; GAAP operating loss improved to $27.8 million from $41.4 million in the fourth quarter; and management guided the second quarter to $10.0 million plus or minus $0.5 million. Stevens also said the company was seeing expanded customer engagements and order backlog. The earnings story had not yet turned into a scale story, but it had turned into a cleaner directional one. [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

That distinction between direction and scale was the key earnings conclusion of the frozen window. The company had not rebuilt revenue to anything close to the 2024 base, but it had begun to replace low-quality volume with a smaller set of higher-power programmes that management believed could carry better long-term economics. The public filings proved the pivot existed. They did not yet prove how large it would become.

chapters.title: Sheridan, Allexandre, Kinzer, and the post-SPAC board
chapters.body:
## The Founder Narrative Ended Earlier Than the Draft Stated

Navitas's leadership history began with its two founders, Gene Sheridan and Dan Kinzer, both alumni of International Rectifier. Sheridan led the company from founding through its early commercial scale-up and public listing; Kinzer carried the technical programme that produced GaNFast. That part of the story was real, but the frozen-window roster was materially different from the one in the earlier draft. By May 23, 2026, neither man held the operating role that older summaries had preserved, and neither remained a director. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power) [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

Kinzer's departure came first. The 2026 proxy said he resigned from his positions as chief operating officer and chief technology officer effective May 1, 2025 and resigned from the board effective May 8, 2025. Navitas also disclosed that it entered into an adviser and consulting arrangement with him focused on gallium-nitride technology, but the operative point for governance was that he did not remain in executive office through the Allexandre transition. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

Sheridan's transition came later and was broader. On August 20, 2025 Navitas announced that Chris Allexandre would become president and chief executive effective September 1, 2025. The company said Sheridan would step down from both the chief-executive role and the board on August 31, 2025. That point mattered because some secondary summaries had treated him as a continuing director. The SEC and IR record did not. [Allexandre appointment release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-names-chris-allexandre-president-and-chief) [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

## Chris Allexandre Was Hired for Scale, Not Founding Continuity

Allexandre arrived from Renesas Electronics, where Navitas said he had served as senior vice-president and general manager of the power division, overseeing a business of about $2.5 billion. The board's message was explicit: the company believed it had moved beyond the stage where a founder-evangelist profile was enough. It wanted a chief executive who had already run a large power-semiconductor operation, dealt with tier-one customers and managed global manufacturing and go-to-market complexity. [Allexandre appointment release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-names-chris-allexandre-president-and-chief)

His first complete reported quarter as chief executive was the first quarter of 2026. In that release, Allexandre described the period as the first clear proof point for Navitas 2.0 and reiterated that the company was focused on four markets: AI data centres, energy and green infrastructure, performance computing and industrial electrification. The phrasing was important because it marked a shift away from the earlier mobile-charger identity without pretending the revenue scale had already caught up. [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The proxy also showed that the board had hard-wired scale-oriented incentives into his compensation. It listed an annual base salary of $520,000, a one-time award of 800,000 time-based RSUs tied to his start date, and a contemplated 2026 performance-stock-unit award with a grant-date value of $2.5 million tied to cumulative revenue goals over the 2026-2028 period. That is useful because it showed the board was not merely asking Allexandre to preserve the story; it was explicitly linking a large share of his economics to revenue conversion. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

## Finance Leadership Also Turned Over

The earlier draft had left Todd Glickman in place as chief financial officer through May 2026. The SEC record showed otherwise. On March 11, 2026 Navitas disclosed that Tonya Stevens had been appointed senior vice-president of finance and chief financial officer effective March 30, 2026. Stevens had joined Navitas as vice-president, corporate controller and chief accounting officer in 2022. The same month, the company disclosed Glickman's resignation effective March 30, 2026 and said he would remain briefly as a non-executive employee through June 30, 2026 to support the transition. [Tonya Stevens 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926026385/tm268482d1_8k.htm) [Todd Glickman 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926029469/tm269070d1_8k.htm)

Stevens's background was more operational and accounting-heavy than the older founding-era finance story. Navitas said she had previously held finance roles at Lattice Semiconductor, Intel and PricewaterhouseCoopers. That change reinforced the broader governance pattern: by spring 2026, the company was replacing much of the founding-era operating layer with executives whose resumes were shaped by scaled public-company finance and manufacturing rather than by start-up formation. [Tonya Stevens 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926026385/tm268482d1_8k.htm)

## The Board Was Not Chaired by Brian Long

The board chapter of the old draft was also stale. The 2026 proxy showed that Richard Hendrix was the chair of the board. Brian Long remained a director, but the proxy described him as the former lead independent director rather than the chair. That distinction mattered because the earlier text had built part of its governance analysis around a board structure that no longer existed. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

The same proxy and related 8-K filings showed a broader board refresh during 2025 and 2026. Cristiano Amoruso was appointed to the board effective May 8, 2025. Gregory Fischer joined in April 2026, and Davin Lee joined effective April 30, 2026. By the frozen snapshot date, the company's director slate had been expanded well beyond the founding pair and the older SPAC-era cast. [Amoruso 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465925043474/tm2514814d1_8k.htm) [Gregory Fischer 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926042619/tm2611717d1_8k.htm) [Davin Lee 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926054482/tm2613278d1_8k.htm)

The proxy also showed that the board's leadership structure had been shaped by a specific April 23, 2025 agreement with Ranbir Singh and SiCPower, LLC. Under that agreement, Hendrix became chair, and the board created an Executive Steering Committee chaired by Singh, initially with Hendrix and Moxam as members; Fischer was added in April 2026 and Moxam stepped down from that committee at the same time. Navitas said the committee had oversight over strategic matters including capital allocation, expense management and certain senior hiring and succession processes. That detail sharpened the governance reading: this was not just a routine board refresh, but a board reorganising itself around capital discipline and strategic oversight during the reset. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

The ownership table underscored that this was still a company with meaningful insider alignment even after the founder exits. The proxy said directors and executive officers as a group beneficially owned 29,046,542 shares, or 12.4 per cent of the Class A stock outstanding on the record date, while Singh alone beneficially owned 18,667,651 shares, or 8.0 per cent. That ownership did not settle the execution debate, but it did mean the board's strategic choices were being made with sizeable insider exposure to the equity outcome. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

The committee map also showed where the board had concentrated its oversight. The proxy said Gary K. Wunderlich, Jr. chaired the audit committee, with Cristiano Amoruso, Richard Hendrix and David Moxam as members, and identified Wunderlich as the audit committee financial expert. David Moxam chaired the compensation committee, with Gregory Fischer, Davin Lee and Brian Long as members. Brian Long chaired the governance and sustainability committee, with Amoruso, Lee and Dipender Saluja serving alongside him. That committee structure matters because it shows the governance build-out had become more institutional than the founder-centric story in the older version implied. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

## As of May 23, 2026, the Roster Looked Like This

| Person | Role as supported by primary filings | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Chris Allexandre | President, chief executive officer and director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Tonya Stevens | Senior vice-president of finance and chief financial officer | [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926026385/tm268482d1_8k.htm) |
| Richard Hendrix | Chair of the board | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Brian Long | Director; former lead independent director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Cristiano Amoruso | Director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| David Moxam | Director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Dipender Saluja | Director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Ranbir Singh | Director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Gary K. Wunderlich, Jr. | Director | [Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm) |
| Gregory Fischer | Director | [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926042619/tm2611717d1_8k.htm) |
| Davin Lee | Director | [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926054482/tm2613278d1_8k.htm) |

The proxy said the board had ten directors standing for election at the 2026 annual meeting, eight of whom were independent. That was a different governance picture from the founder-heavy roster in the old draft. It was closer to the board of a small public semiconductor company trying to institutionalise itself while still leaning heavily on one strategic theme: AI infrastructure power. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

The same proxy also made plain that Navitas had formalised the usual public-company checks and incentives around that board. Non-employee directors received a $45,000 annual retainer, with additional fees for committee service; the former lead independent director role carried a $20,000 annual fee, audit committee service carried a $10,000 fee per member with double pay for the chair, and compensation and governance committee service carried separate retainers as well. Those details are mundane, but they matter because they showed a governance structure that had moved beyond founder informality and into standard public-company process at the same time that the strategy itself was being rebuilt. [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

## What the Corrected Governance Story Implied

Once the errors were removed, the leadership chapter became less romantic and more legible. The company did not carry seamless founder continuity into 2026. It replaced its CEO, its CFO and its chair structure inside twelve months, while the technical co-founder exited operating and board roles even earlier than the chief executive did. That did not invalidate the strategic case, but it did change the risk profile. The execution of Navitas 2.0 was being asked of a materially different leadership team from the one that had taken the company public. [Allexandre appointment release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-names-chris-allexandre-president-and-chief) [Tonya Stevens 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926026385/tm268482d1_8k.htm) [2026 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000110465926058742/tm2613272d3_def14a.htm)

chapters.title: NVIDIA, mobile OEMs, foundry partnerships, and HALEU-style scarcity of GaN capacity
chapters.body:
## The Customer List Started in Chargers and Moved Up the Stack

Navitas's early disclosed customer base looked like that of a company winning on charger density and efficiency. In the 2021 SPAC materials, the company named customers and partners including Dell, Lenovo, LG, Xiaomi, OPPO, Amazon and Belkin. That list was valuable not because all of those relationships necessarily carried equal revenue weight, but because it confirmed that GaNFast had already crossed from engineering promise into volume consumer power applications before the company became public. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power)

By 2025, the named ecosystem had shifted. In April 2025 Navitas announced a partnership with Great Wall for a next-generation 400V DC power architecture for AI data centres, highlighting a 2.5 kW DC-DC converter using GaNFast ICs. A few days later it announced a partnership with GigaDevice to combine power and control technologies through a joint laboratory. In May 2025 NVIDIA then disclosed the 800V HVDC collaboration for Kyber rack-scale systems powering Rubin Ultra GPUs. Those announcements did not turn the company into an AI-infrastructure incumbent overnight, but they showed that the customer-development effort was migrating from adapters and handsets to system-level power chains. [Great Wall release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-partners-great-wall-next-generation-400v-dc-power) [GigaDevice release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-gigadevice-announce-partnership-combine-power-control) [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

That migration was reinforced by the 2025-2026 hardware cadence. In the fourth-quarter 2025 release, Navitas said it had accelerated customer sampling of 100V and 650V GaN solutions for 800V HVDC data-centre architecture and announced a 10 kW 800V-to-50V all-GaN platform. In the first-quarter 2026 release it said it had demonstrated a 20 kW 800V-to-6V board at NVIDIA GTC and a 250 kW solid-state transformer with EPFL. Those are the kinds of references that infrastructure customers, rather than handset OEMs, tend to care about. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## The Public Record on Revenue Mix Matched That Customer Shift

The earnings releases confirmed that the company was acting on that customer repositioning rather than merely marketing it. In the 2025 annual results, Navitas said mobile and consumer had dropped to less than 25 per cent of fourth-quarter revenue while high-power markets had risen above 50 per cent. In the first quarter of 2026, management said high-power markets represented a large majority of revenue and had grown 35 per cent year on year. The customer map was therefore changing even though the absolute revenue base was still small. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The dossier had previously treated December 2024 as the turning point. The primary record made May 2025 the better marker, because that was when the named NVIDIA relationship entered the public record. The company later said it had demonstrated a 20 kW 800V HVDC to 6V power delivery board at GTC in 2026, which showed the relationship progressing into engineering hardware rather than remaining an abstract collaboration. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

## The Supply Chain Was Becoming the Strategic Constraint

The manufacturing side of the story was at least as important as the customer side. Navitas had long relied on third-party manufacturing partners, beginning with the TSMC and Amkor relationships announced in 2017. That arrangement made sense when the company was primarily serving chargers and adapters. It became more delicate once the sales pitch shifted toward AI infrastructure, where customers cared about geographic concentration, long-term capacity and domestic sourcing. [TSMC and Amkor manufacturing release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-announces-tsmc-amkor-manufacturing-partnerships)

The primary filings disclosed just how concentrated the starting point was. In the June 30, 2025 Form 10-Q, Navitas said its sole supplier of GaN wafers had notified it that it planned to cease GaN production in July 2027. The same filing said Navitas had qualified Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation as a new supplier in the fourth quarter of 2025 and expected initial mass production in the first half of 2026. That was a more specific and more consequential supply-chain disclosure than the earlier draft had captured: the company was not merely diversifying foundries in the abstract, it was working against an explicit sunset from its existing GaN wafer source. [Q2 2025 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000181/nvts-20250630.htm)

The July 2025 Powerchip announcement gave that transition a commercial wrapper. Navitas said the new relationship would support 200 mm manufacturing and lower costs, and it tied the move directly to high-growth markets including AI data centres, EVs and solar. In November 2025 the company followed with a strategic partnership with GlobalFoundries aimed at U.S.-based GaN production in Burlington, Vermont, with development work beginning in early 2026 and production targeted for late 2026. That gave Navitas a two-step supply-chain answer: a near-term alternative foundry in Taiwan and a later U.S. manufacturing foothold. [PSMC release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/cbb9fa0e-1a41-463e-b71c-1a5b1145678d) [GlobalFoundries partnership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000217/nvts-20251120.htm)

The year-end 2025 release made clear why those manufacturing moves were part of the commercial story rather than a separate operations story. Management tied the November 2025 private placement, the GlobalFoundries partnership and the new 100V and 650V GaN sampling effort together as supports for the acceleration into higher-power markets. By then the supply chain had become a visible input into customer conversion rather than a backend detail. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

## Silicon Carbide Added Breadth but Also Dependence

The SiC side of the supply chain was less publicly named. Navitas's filings described external foundry and supply dependencies for silicon-carbide products, but they did not name the principal SiC wafer supplier in the same way that the GaN transition became visible through the TSMC-to-Powerchip shift. What could be said from primary sources was narrower: the GeneSiC acquisition gave Navitas higher-voltage product depth, and later product releases repeatedly paired those devices with GaN in system-level infrastructure applications. The filings did not support a claim that SiC was already the main driver of the AI-data-centre revenue line by the frozen snapshot date. [GeneSiC completion release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-completes-acquisition-genesic-semiconductor) [PCIM 2025 release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-showcases-advances-gan-and-sic-technologies-including)

## The Supply Chain Had Become Part of the Product Pitch

By May 23, 2026, Navitas was selling more than device performance. It was also selling an answer to procurement questions that large infrastructure customers would inevitably ask: who fabricated the wafers, whether there was a second source, when 200 mm capacity would be available, and whether any U.S.-based manufacturing path existed. That was why the PSMC and GlobalFoundries announcements mattered so much. The customer story and the supply-chain story had converged. [PSMC release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/cbb9fa0e-1a41-463e-b71c-1a5b1145678d) [GlobalFoundries partnership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000217/nvts-20251120.htm)

chapters.title: Where Navitas sits against Infineon CoolGaN, Power Integrations, ON Semi, STMicro, Wolfspeed
chapters.body:
## Navitas Was Strategically Visible but Financially Small

By the frozen snapshot date, Navitas occupied an unusual competitive position. It had a named collaboration with NVIDIA on 800V HVDC architecture, a differentiated pure-play wide-bandgap identity and a product story that combined GaN and SiC. But it also had only $45.9 million of full-year 2025 revenue and $8.6 million of first-quarter 2026 revenue. In other words, it was competing for attention in an industry segment dominated by companies with much larger income statements and much deeper manufacturing bases. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial) [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc)

The scale gap was clear in primary-source disclosures:

| Company | Period | Reported revenue | Primary source |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Navitas | FY2025 | $45.9 million | [Navitas FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) |
| Power Integrations | Q1 2026 | $108.3 million | [Power Integrations Q1 2026](https://investors.power.com/news/news-details/2026/Power-Integrations-Reports-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx) |
| onsemi | Q1 2026 | $1.513 billion | [onsemi Q1 2026](https://www.onsemi.com/company/news-media/press-announcements/en/onsemi-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) |
| STMicroelectronics | Q1 2026 | $3.095 billion | [ST Q1 2026](https://investors.st.com/news-releases/news-release-details/stmicroelectronics-reports-2026-first-quarter-financial-results) |
| Infineon | FY2024 | EUR 14.955 billion | [Infineon FY2024](https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/about-infineon/press/press-releases/2024/INFXX202411-020.html) |

That table did not prove those competitors were all fighting in identical product niches, but it did show the practical asymmetry. Navitas was trying to establish a position in the same broad electrification and AI-power transition with a fraction of the resources.

## The GaN Field Was Consolidating Around Bigger Balance Sheets

Infineon was a good example of the direction of travel. In 2023 it agreed to acquire GaN Systems for US$830 million, a transaction it said would strengthen its GaN systems capabilities and accelerate its roadmap. By late 2024 Infineon was still speaking about GaN as a strategic growth vector inside a revenue base that dwarfed Navitas's entire company. That did not make Infineon a direct substitute for Navitas in every socket, but it did mean that one of the world's largest power-semiconductor companies had decided that GaN was important enough to buy engineering depth rather than wait to build it organically. [Infineon GaN Systems acquisition](https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/about-infineon/press/press-releases/2023/INFXX202303-073.html) [Infineon FY2024](https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/about-infineon/press/press-releases/2024/INFXX202411-020.html)

Power Integrations represented a different kind of rival. It was much smaller than Infineon but still much larger than Navitas, and it had long specialised in highly integrated power-conversion products. Its first-quarter 2026 revenue of $108.3 million underscored the gap between a scaled integrated-power supplier and Navitas's still-resetting revenue base. The overlap mattered because both companies sold the idea that more functions should be integrated at the device level rather than left to the customer. [Power Integrations Q1 2026](https://investors.power.com/news/news-details/2026/Power-Integrations-Reports-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## The Silicon-Carbide Incumbents Were Larger and More Vertically Ambitious

On the SiC side, STMicroelectronics and onsemi were operating at a wholly different scale. ST reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.095 billion and used its release to discuss the datacentre and industrial opportunity alongside a broad automotive and industrial base. onsemi reported $1.513 billion of first-quarter 2026 revenue and said its AI-data-centre business had grown more than 30 per cent sequentially. Neither disclosure put the companies into the exact same competitive slot as Navitas, but both made plain that the market Navitas wanted to enter was already crowded with larger vendors that could fund capacity, qualification and customer support from much broader businesses. [ST Q1 2026](https://investors.st.com/news-releases/news-release-details/stmicroelectronics-reports-2026-first-quarter-financial-results) [onsemi Q1 2026](https://www.onsemi.com/company/news-media/press-announcements/en/onsemi-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

Wolfspeed showed the opposite risk: what could happen when a pure-play materials and power story tried to carry too much capital intensity. In September 2025 Wolfspeed said it had completed a financial restructuring that reduced total debt by about 70 per cent and annual cash interest payments by about 60 per cent. For Navitas, which remained fabless, the lesson was double-edged. The company avoided Wolfspeed-style balance-sheet strain, but it also lacked Wolfspeed's control over core substrate and device manufacturing. [Wolfspeed restructuring release](https://investor.wolfspeed.com/news/news-details/2025/Wolfspeed-Successfully-Completes-Financial-Restructuring-Emerges-as-Financially-Stronger-Company-Well-Positioned-in-Silicon-Carbide-Market/default.aspx)

Texas Instruments illustrated a parallel point on the GaN side. In October 2024 TI said it had begun producing GaN-based power semiconductors at Aizu, Japan, quadrupling internal GaN manufacturing capacity across its U.S. and Japan factories, and in March 2025 it introduced integrated 650V GaN power stages for modern data centres. TI was not a pure-play power-device company in the Navitas mould, but its disclosures showed that large analog groups were not standing aside while GaN moved into higher-power infrastructure. [TI GaN manufacturing release](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2024/2024-10-24-texas-instruments-expands-internal-manufacturing-for-gallium-nitride--gan--semiconductors--quadrupling-capacity.html) [TI data-centre GaN release](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2025/2025-03-17-new-power-management-chips-from-ti-maximize-protection--density-and-efficiency-for-modern-data-centers.html?HQS=app-lp-pwr-dce2025_tps1685_apec2025-bhp-pr-null-wwe)

That made manufacturing model part of the competitive comparison. Infineon, ST, onsemi, TI and Wolfspeed each had some combination of internal manufacturing scale, broader product portfolios or vertical integration. Navitas's answer was different: it stayed fabless and tried to compensate with a more focused architecture story plus external manufacturing relationships through TSMC, Powerchip and GlobalFoundries. The advantage of that approach was lower capital intensity. The disadvantage was that manufacturing control and supply assurance were necessarily shared with partners at the very moment when AI-infrastructure customers were making those issues more central. [TSMC and Amkor manufacturing release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-announces-tsmc-amkor-manufacturing-partnerships) [PSMC release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/static-files/cbb9fa0e-1a41-463e-b71c-1a5b1145678d) [GlobalFoundries partnership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821769/000182176925000217/nvts-20251120.htm)

## What Navitas Actually Had That Rivals Did Not

The easiest way to overstate Navitas was to mistake the NVIDIA collaboration for already-booked commercial scale. The easiest way to understate it was to ignore what the public record uniquely gave it. NVIDIA did not merely buy a component off the shelf; it named Navitas as a collaborator in next-generation 800V HVDC architecture for Kyber rack-scale systems powering Rubin Ultra. Navitas later said it was supporting that architecture with 100V GaN, 650V GaN and high-voltage SiC, then accelerated customer sampling of those parts, then demonstrated a 20 kW 800V HVDC to 6V board and a 250 kW solid-state transformer in 2026. That sequence put the company into the architecture layer of the AI-power discussion in a way that most peers had not publicly disclosed for themselves. [NVIDIA collaboration release](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nvidia-selects-navitas-collaborate-next-generation-800-v-hvdc) [October 2025 NVIDIA update](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-supports-800-vdc-power-architecture-nvidias-next) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

Navitas also had a cleaner identity than most of its rivals. Every public-company dollar and every product roadmap page pointed toward wide-bandgap power. There was no legacy microcontroller business, no automotive MCU franchise, no silicon MOSFET cash cow to defend. That focus could still prove insufficient, but it was real. [Navitas SPAC announcement](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-industry-leader-gallium-nitride-gan-power)

The company also had a more concentrated end-market narrative than it had when it came public. By the first quarter of 2026, management was explicitly framing the opportunity around AI data centres, energy and green infrastructure, performance computing and industrial electrification, and it had already said in the 2024 annual results that its highest design-win growth rates were in data centre and EV. That did not solve the scale problem, but it did mean Navitas was competing with a deliberately narrowed commercial target rather than trying to win every wide-bandgap socket at once. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)

The company did, however, warn investors not to confuse pipeline language with firm demand. In both its 2024 and 2025 annual results releases, Navitas said customer pipeline and design wins did not represent customer orders, were not proxies for backlog and should not be treated as estimates of future revenue. That disclaimer is central to understanding the competitive position: Navitas had proven relevance, but it had not yet proven a revenue outcome equal to the attention. [FY2024 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year) [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0)

## The Competitive Question Was Monetisation, Not Visibility

The competitive chapter therefore narrowed to a simple test. Could Navitas turn architectural relevance into enough repeat revenue to matter before larger competitors closed whatever functional gap still separated them from GaNFast and the company's combined GaN-plus-SiC pitch. The filings through May 23, 2026 established visibility, partnerships, manufacturing moves and mix change. They did not yet establish a revenue outcome commensurate with the ambition. [FY2025 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-0) [Q1 2026 results](https://ir.navitassemi.com/news-releases/news-release-details/navitas-semiconductor-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial)
